text:
anjali: Quick notes from today's sampling-aware bring-up for q-llama-70b-8bit. High-level: ~1.9x p50 decode speedup with adaptive prefetcher, but small quality drops on a couple QA/knowledge benchmarks. Posting quick logs and configs below.

mike: Nice. Which benchmarks saw regressions and how big are we talking?

anjali: TL;DR numbers: NQ exact match -1.1 pts, TriviaQA F1 -0.7, Human eval subset (200 prompts) preference ~48% vs baseline. Throughput p50 went from 210 tok/s -> 400 tok/s on the same instance. Latency tail unchanged for short prompts.

lee: Do you have the eval commands/config? Can we reproduce locally?

anjali: Repro snippet:
```
EXPERIMENT=model.q70b.8bit.prefetch_v2
BATCH=1
MAXLEN=512
KV_PREFETCH=true
SEED=42
python eval/run_eval.py --model $EXPERIMENT --batch $BATCH --maxlen $MAXLEN --dataset triviaqa, noq --seed $SEED --log_dir /tmp/q70b_prefetch_v2
```
Config notes: prefetcher uses a scoring window of 32 tokens, opportunistic spec-fetch when entropy < 3.2, fallback to baseline policy on timeout=50ms.

mike: Good. The entropy threshold is interesting — did you try sweeping it? Could be a source of bias towards low-diverse continuations.

anjali: Ran a quick sweep (3.0, 3.2, 3.6). 3.2 was best perf/quality tradeoff. At 3.0 we saw bigger drop on TriviaQA (~-1.8 F1) but slightly more speed. 3.6 nearly matches quality but loses some speed (~1.55x).

lee: Any pattern in failures? Long-context vs short? Specific prompt types?

anjali: Failures concentrated on multi-hop factual prompts and prompts relying on rare token completions. Example failure (shortened):
"Given the sequence of events in 1999, which city hosted the summit where X happened?"
Baseline: correctly outputs city. Prefetch_v2: outputs nearby city/ambiguous name. Hypothesis: prefetch biases towards higher-prob tokens in early kv-window, losing later-disambiguating tokens.

mike: Makes sense. We should add a targeted holdout of multi-hop questions and a few adversarial prompts to the gating eval. Also run bootstrap to get CI on the human eval drop.

anjali: Agreed. Plan: 1) Run 10x bootstrap on 2k human eval subset, 2) add 1k adversarial/multi-hop holdout, 3) baseline vs prefetch_v2 A/B with traffic shadowing (10% traffic) for 24h, 4) test entropy sweep with smaller steps [3.1,3.25,3.4].

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for model.q70b.8bit.prefetch_v2 -> route: canary-10pct at 2026-03-20T16:15Z.

lee: Thanks. One more ops ask: can we log token-entropy deltas when prefetch triggers? That will help debug early bias.

anjali: Yep adding token-entropy-delta logs and per-request trace id. Also will attach sample failing prompts to the issue.

mike: If CI shows non-significant drop but human preference still ~48%, consider running a small RL-based calibration or soft-rescoring on the prefetched continuation. But only after we confirm stability.

anjali: Yep — adding rescoring A/B to the backlog. For now throttling the canary to 5% if we see >1.5 pt drop on NQ.

lee: ack. Thanks for the notes. :thumbsup:

anjali: I'll post the full eval logs and the holdout set link once upload finishes (/gs/q70b/prefetch_v2/).
